|  | ${x}^{2}$ | ${x}^{1}$ | ${x}^{0}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $4$ | $4$ | $-17$ | $4$ |
|  | $↓$ | $16$ | $-4$ |
|  | $4$ | $-1$ | $0$ |

So from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\frac{4{x}^{2}-17x+4}{x-4}=4x-1.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{4{x}^{2}-17x+4}{x-4}\,\text{d}x & =\int (4x-1)\text{d}x \\  & =4\int x\,\text{d}x-\int \text{d}x \\  & =4\cdot \frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}-x+C \\  & =2{x}^{2}-x+C.\end{aligned}
$$

We first need to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder parts, which we can do using synthetic division.

We draw up a synthetic division table:

$$
\begin{aligned} & {x}^{3} & {x}^{2} & {x}^{1} & {x}^{0} \\ 2 & 1 & 0 & 1 & -1 \\  & ↓ & 2 & 4 & 10 \\  & 1 & 2 & 5 & 9\end{aligned}
$$

So from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\frac{{x}^{3}+x-1}{x-2}={x}^{2}+2x+5+\frac{9}{x-2}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{{x}^{3}+x-1}{x-2}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{2}+2x+5+\frac{9}{x-2})\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x+2{\int }_{0}^{1}x\,\text{d}x+5{\int }_{0}^{1}\text{d}x+9{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{x-2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}\,{|}_{0}^{1}+{x}^{2}\,{|}_{0}^{1}+5x\,{|}_{0}^{1}+9\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-2|\,{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}({1}^{3}-{0}^{3})+({1}^{2}+{0}^{2})+5(1-0)+9(\operatorname{ln}⁡|1-2|-\operatorname{ln}⁡|0-2|) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}+1+5+9(\operatorname{ln}⁡1-\operatorname{ln}⁡2) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}+6-9\operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\  & =\frac{19}{3}-9\operatorname{ln}⁡2.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
First, we pull out the factor of $6$ from the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1/12}^{0}\frac{2x+1}{6x+1}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-1/12}^{0}\frac{2x+1}{6(x+\frac{1}{6})}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{6}{\int }_{-1/12}^{0}\frac{2x+1}{(x+\frac{1}{6})}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we draw up our synthetic division table to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder.

$$
\begin{aligned} & x & {x}^{0} \\ -\frac{1}{6} & 2 & 1 \\  & ↓ & -\frac{1}{3} \\  & 2 & \frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

So from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2x+1}{(x+\frac{1}{6})} & =2+\frac{(\frac{2}{3})}{(x+\frac{1}{6})} \\  & =2+\frac{4}{6x+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1/12}^{0}\frac{2x+1}{6x+1}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{6}{\int }_{-1/12}^{0}(2+\frac{4}{6x+1})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[2{\int }_{-1/12}^{0}\text{d}x+4{\int }_{-1/12}^{0}\frac{1}{6x+1}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}{[2x+\frac{4}{6}\operatorname{ln}⁡|6x+1|]}_{-1/12}^{0} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}{[2x+\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|6x+1|]}_{-1/12}^{0} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[2(0-(-\frac{1}{12}))+\frac{2}{3}(\operatorname{ln}⁡|6(0)+1|-\operatorname{ln}⁡|6(-\frac{1}{12})+1|)] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[2(\frac{1}{12})+\frac{2}{3}(\operatorname{ln}⁡1-\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{2}))] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[\frac{1}{6}+\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡2] \\  & =\frac{1}{36}(1+4\operatorname{ln}⁡2).\end{aligned}
$$

First, we pull out the factor of $5$ from the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{8x-3}{5x+1}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{8x-3}{5(x+1/5)}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{5}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{8x-3}{(x+1/5)}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we draw up our synthetic division table to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder.

|  | ${x}^{1}$ | ${x}^{0}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $-\frac{1}{5}$ | $8$ | $-3$ |
|  | $↓$ | $-\frac{8}{5}$ |
|  | $8$ | $-\frac{23}{5}$ |

So, from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{8x-3}{(x+1/5)} & =8-\frac{(23/5)}{(x+1/5)} \\  & =8-\frac{23}{5x+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{8x-3}{5x+1}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{5}{\int }_{0}^{1}(8-\frac{23}{5x+1})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[8{\int }_{0}^{1}\text{d}x-23{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{5x+1}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}{[8x-\frac{23}{5}\operatorname{ln}⁡|5x+1|]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[8(1-0)-\frac{23}{5}(\operatorname{ln}⁡|6|-\operatorname{ln}⁡|1|)] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[8-\frac{23\operatorname{ln}⁡6}{5}] \\  & =\frac{8}{5}-\frac{23}{25}\operatorname{ln}⁡(6).\end{aligned}
$$
